s.diag.h: From bank statement to rent account
s.diag.p: One line of the CAMT.053 file is checked, matched to a tenancy and posted to the rent account. You can split or reverse an entry.
s.g1.p: Finalized statements and records can no longer be changed.
s.g2.p: You fix mistakes with a reversal and a correction, without deleting records.
s.g4.p: Access to a person’s data and erasure requests with retention checks. Protected records remain; final erasure after expiry is not currently automatic.
s.g5.p: Organizations are separated by row-level database rules and permissions. Privileged operational access requires additional organizational controls.
s.g6.p: Neither this site nor the app uses analytics trackers.
s.m1: Properties and units with year built, areas, meters and meter readings
s.m2: Leases with base rent, operating-cost advance payments and deposit
s.m3: Graduated rent, index-linked rent and rent changes from a set date
s.m4: Rent charges prorated by day, a rent account for each tenancy, open items
s.m5: Tenant changes and deposits: agreed, paid, repaid
s.m6: Betriebskostenabrechnung (operating-cost statement) per lease, as a PDF
s.q1.a: Nothing. That goes for the hosted service once it launches and for installing it on your own server. The source code is on GitHub under AGPL-3.0. You can download it there for your own installation.
s.q2.a: Yes. In addition to CSV, DATEV and PDF outputs, an organization archive contains authorized records and original files. It does not include all internal evidence; access and re-import have limitations. A complete service-exit handover needs separate verification as described in the DPA draft.
s.q3.a: Current source limits the free hosted service to 20 properties, 200 units and 2 GiB of document storage per organization. These hosted quotas do not apply to self-hosting; usable scale also depends on hardware and data volume.
s.q3.q: How many units can Verwalino handle?
s.q4.a: Yes. Docker Compose starts Verwalino together with PostgreSQL, on a laptop just as on a server.
s.q4.q: Does it run on my laptop?
s.q5.a: No. Optional document analysis and property questions are included in the hosted launch model. Customers choose and contract with their own AI provider and supply their own key. Current source supports OpenAI, Anthropic and OpenAI-compatible endpoints. Document text, page images, questions and context may be transmitted; content processing requires a stored key. Model discovery can contact the provider with a key entered before saving. The recorded confirmation when saving the key still requires implementation (#617); see the privacy notice and DPA drafts.
s.q6.a: The hosted server is at Contabo in Germany according to the operator decision. Email, backups and optional analysis services require separate checks; Germany is not a promise covering every data flow. Outstanding recipient details are identified in the legal drafts. Self-hosting operators determine their own processing.
s.r1.p: Each lease gets a statement that accounts for partial rental periods and vacancies. Costs are split by floor area, co-ownership shares (MEA), units, people, consumption or by hand. The statement takes the advance payments from the payments you posted. One run creates the drafts for the whole property; you check and finalize each statement, and then get its PDF and a suggestion for the new advance payment.
s.r2.p: Split into a base share and a consumption share, or you use the statement from your metering company.
s.r3.p: The Hausgeld the owners have paid is already included, and the asset report is modelled on § 28(4) WEG. The annual budget and the annual statement come out as PDFs for the owners' meeting.
s.r4.p: Import bank statements as CSV or CAMT.053 (XML or ZIP). Verwalino first shows what would be booked, spots transactions imported twice and suggests rent accounts; only what you confirm gets posted. You can split a payment across several accounts or reverse it.
s.r5.p: Collect monthly rent by direct debit: manage mandates and your creditor ID, and create the pain.008 file for your bank.
s.r6.p: Three reminder levels with a fee and late-payment interest (base rate plus 5 percentage points, § 288 BGB; you enter the base rate). The reminder run first shows who would get a reminder; the ones you select become drafts, from which you create the PDFs.
s.r7.p: Export accounting entries for your tax advisor in DATEV format (SKR03 or SKR04), plus CSV and an annual summary for each property.
s.r8.p: Upload an invoice, enter the amount and BetrKV cost type, and the cost item is done. Text recognition and e-invoices (XML) are handled by a background service that is currently switched off.

self.intro: Verwalino runs with Docker Compose and PostgreSQL on your server or laptop. The steps below apply to the current state on GitHub.
self.requirements.title: Prerequisites
self.requirements.body: Linux or macOS with Bash, OpenSSL, Docker Engine 24 or later (or Docker Desktop) and Docker Compose 2.24 or later. You do not need Python, Node or a separate proxy for the first installation.
self.commands.title: Three commands from the checkout
self.init.title: What init creates
self.init.body: `init` creates five different random 256-bit keys in the private file `.env.selfhost` (file mode 0600). Back up this file; an existing one is not overwritten. `start` builds the image from the checkout, waits for the database, runs the migrations and starts the app, locally at `http://127.0.0.1:18080`.
self.admin.title: The first administrator
self.admin.body: The third command creates the organization and its administrator and asks for the password twice without showing it. There is no default password, and existing users are left as they are. On an empty installation, `start` can instead print a `/setup` address and, separately, a one-time token valid for 24 hours. This browser route has not been released yet.
self.https.title: HTTPS with Caddy
self.https.body: For an installation reachable from the internet, choose HTTPS when you run `init`: `--https` `verwaltung.example.org`. The domain must point to the server, and ports 80 and 443 must be free. Caddy redirects HTTP to HTTPS and gets the certificates. Sign in through the HTTPS address and don’t expose the local HTTP port to the internet. Check that the certificate has been issued and the HTTPS address is reachable.
self.backup.title: Back up before changes
self.backup.body: Before an upgrade, run `bash scripts/self-host.sh backup` to archive the database and documents. `.env.selfhost` is not included; keep that file separately and encrypted. To restore, stop the app, load the archive with `restore` and start it again. Try this once on another machine so you know it works. There is no update command yet, and an older image does not roll back the database schema.
self.limits.title: What this installation does not yet support
self.limits.body: In the installation described here, email sending (SMTP), the optional document analysis and automatic invoice OCR are turned off; you enter invoices by hand. The signed public image is not published yet; `start` builds it from the checkout. Installation on a fresh server and use with a real domain and TLS are not yet cleared for production.
self.unreleased.title: Planned releases
self.unreleased.body: The source code is on GitHub under AGPL-3.0. Backup, restore and the doctor command are in the checkout. These parts are still missing or not yet released:
self.repository.body: `DEPLOY.md` in the public GitHub repository contains the full guide.

draft.privacy.controller.title: 1. Controller and scope
draft.privacy.controller.body: {operator.name}, {operator.street}, {operator.city}, {operator.country}, represented by {operator.director}, is controller for this website and hosted-service account, contract and operational data. Contact: {operator.privacyEmail}. This notice covers verwalino.de and app.verwalino.de; self-hosting operators are responsible for their own processing. Christian Kunkel handles rights requests, security and incidents. [TO SUPPLY Q12: absence deputy’s name.] The owner documents the DPO and DPIA duty assessments himself. [ASSESSMENT EVIDENCE REQUIRED: If appointment is required, add the DPO’s contact details before approval.]
draft.privacy.hosting.title: 2. Website, hosting and connection data
draft.privacy.hosting.body: The website serves static pages and local fonts. Your browser supplies connection data needed for delivery, such as its network address and requested resource. Website code contains no analytics, advertising or external font services. Contabo remains the host; the owner concludes its processing agreement before launch. [TO SUPPLY Q02: data-centre location from the hosting contract.] Complete legal entity, address, access locations and further recipients from that contract. The purpose is service delivery and security, based on Article 6(1)(f) GDPR following a documented balancing assessment. The decided policy retains server logs for 14 days from creation. [IMPLEMENTATION REQUIRED: Enforcement and evidence of this period in every log store.]
draft.privacy.account.title: 3. Registration, account and contact
draft.privacy.account.body: Registration processes the organization name, your name, email address and password; a password hash and confirmation-token hash are stored. Roles, preferences, timestamps and security data are also processed. Contact details may instead be supplied by your organization administrator. Purposes are setup, login, account administration, necessary messages and support. Article 6(1)(b) GDPR applies where you personally are the contracting party or request pre-contractual steps; for a company customer’s employees and representatives, Article 6(1)(f) may support orderly provision and security of the service. Legally required handling of privacy requests is based on Article 6(1)(c) with Articles 12–22 GDPR. Required fields are necessary for setup and login; an account cannot be provided without them. No automated decision about you within Article 22 GDPR is made. [IMPLEMENTATION REQUIRED: Versioned electronic assent to terms and DPA with annexes at signup before first data entry, information delivery and durable contract confirmation. Existing email confirmation does not record this.]
draft.privacy.properties.title: 4. Your property manager’s data
draft.privacy.properties.body: For management data entered by customers, fogu generally acts as processor under Article 28 GDPR. This includes tenancy, ownership, contact, bank, payment, accounting, consumption, document and communication data and evidence. A private landlord is also controller where determining processing purposes and means; letting does not fall within exclusively personal or household activity. A self-managing WEG can likewise be controller. Consumer status does not remove these duties. For representation or management for third parties, record the actual roles and instruction chain. The customer determines lawful bases and informs individuals; fogu forwards requests and assists. Own account and operational purposes are separate. Attachments may contain sensitive data; comprehensive filtering is not promised. Basis: Articles 2(2)(c), 4(7) and 28 GDPR, https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2016/679/oj.
draft.privacy.storage.title: 5. Cookies and browser storage
draft.privacy.storage.body: The website sets no cookies. After use of the theme control, verwalino-theme in local storage preserves the requested appearance for later visits without an application expiry; it can be cleared in browser settings. Language follows the URL. The app uses hv_session for login, default two hours, with HttpOnly and SameSite=Lax; Secure must be ensured for HTTPS operation. Tab-bound session storage holds confirmation and password-reset tokens during their flows and an economic-plan form draft with user/organization context to continue entry. Tokens are removed on success or final invalidity, the draft when the form closes; session storage generally ends with the tab session. No tracking is used and no consent banner is planned (Q13). [COUNSEL REVIEW: The section 25(2)(2) TDDDG exception must cover each explicitly requested, strictly necessary storage purpose, particularly theme and form draft. Otherwise resolve this conflict before approval; the owner’s decision is not consent.] Source: https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/ttdsg/__25.html.
draft.privacy.email.title: 6. Email and recipients
draft.privacy.email.body: Account confirmation, password recovery and necessary service messages use an EU mail provider under a processing agreement. [TO SUPPLY Q03: mail provider.] Before approval document its legal entity, address, processing/access locations, sub-processors and retention contractually. Customer-triggered document messages contain the recipient, message and PDF, sent on customer instructions. Transport TLS is intended, not end-to-end encryption. Other recipients are authorized staff, necessary advisers and authorities where legally required or for lawful claims. Bases for own purposes are in section 3; customer mail is governed by instructions and the DPA.
draft.privacy.rights.title: 10. Your rights
draft.privacy.rights.body: Subject to statutory conditions you may request access, rectification, erasure, restriction and portability (Articles 15–20 GDPR). You may object to Article 6(1)(f) processing on grounds relating to your particular situation (Article 21); objection to direct marketing would be possible at any time. You may withdraw consent for the future without affecting earlier lawful processing. Contact: {operator.privacyEmail}. We normally respond within one month; any permitted extension of up to two further months is explained within the first month. We request only necessary identity-verification information. For customer data we assist the relevant controller; statutory exceptions, including records lawfully subject to retention, may prevent erasure. A technical deletion restriction alone is not a statutory exception.
draft.privacy.authority.title: 11. Complaints
draft.privacy.authority.body: Article 77 GDPR gives you the right to complain to a supervisory authority, particularly where you live, work or the alleged infringement occurred. The operator’s named authority is the Unabhängiges Datenschutzzentrum Saarland; contact and complaint channels: https://www.datenschutz.saarland.de. You do not have to contact us first.
draft.terms.scope.title: 1. Provider, eligible customers and service
draft.terms.scope.body: The free hosted Verwalino service is provided by {operator.name}, {operator.street}, {operator.city}, represented by {operator.director}; contact: {operator.email}, telephone as stated in the imprint. It supports rental, WEG and SEV management in separate organizations. Customers may be businesses, private landlords and homeowners’ associations, including consumers. Contract purpose and the actual contracting party determine consumer status; professional representation does not automatically make a WEG a business. The service replaces neither legal/tax advice nor review of results. The project is not yet approved for public use with real management data. AGPL-3.0 governs source code; these terms govern hosting. Basis: sections 13, 14 BGB; BGH VIII ZR 243/13 of 25 March 2015 (sources below).
draft.terms.free.title: 3. Free service and limits
draft.terms.free.body: Use is gratuitous: EUR 0, no subscription or setup fee and no minimum term. A paid contract requires a separate express agreement. Current source limits per organization: 2 GiB document storage, 25 MiB per upload, 20 properties and 200 units; usage and limits appear in the app. Customers bear their own internet/device costs. Optional AI functions are included at hosted launch through the provider the customer chooses and contracts with directly, using its own key; provider fees are borne by the customer. The customer is responsible for the provider’s processing agreement, locations and exclusion of training, without removing fogu’s own statutory duties. The DPA governs instructed transmission. [IMPLEMENTATION REQUIRED #617: Recorded confirmation when storing the key; not implemented yet. COUNSEL REVIEW: Role allocation, including private landlords and WEGs.] No fee does not remove privacy, security, return or mandatory consumer duties.
draft.terms.availability.title: 4. Operation and outages
draft.terms.availability.body: No specific availability percentage or continuous support coverage is promised. Significant planned outages are announced beforehand where possible; necessary security measures may take effect immediately. Send faults and complaints to {operator.email}; Christian Kunkel and the deputy to be named in the privacy notice handle them. This description does not exclude agreed protection/return duties or statutory performance, defect or update rights. Operational and recovery evidence is required before approval.
draft.terms.duties.title: 5. Customer duties
draft.terms.duties.body: The customer manages permissions, protects credentials and processes only data supported by a legal basis and any required consent. It checks calculations, assignments and documents before professional use or dispatch and reports detected errors. It avoids unnecessarily sensitive management data. Customer review does not remove the provider’s own duties. External analysis services may be used only after the approval procedure described in the DPA.
draft.terms.data.title: 6. Data, export and handover
draft.terms.data.body: At service end the customer receives a complete, readable export of management data due for return, including originals and necessary relationships, followed by erasure under section 8. Other tenants’ data or others’ credentials are not disclosed. [IMPLEMENTATION REQUIRED: The existing permission-filtered export is not yet complete return; lawfully supplement missing evidence due for return and verify handover.] Currently the organization export is a .tar.gz with authorized JSONL data, checksum manifest, originals and payment/cost CSV. Download is available for 24 hours while authorization continues and is not itself encrypted. Size, permission and integrity limits may prevent re-import. Export alone does not guarantee a tax-compliant migration. Customers protect received archives; fogu’s own backup duties remain.
draft.terms.termination.title: 7. Termination, shutdown and account access
draft.terms.termination.body: The contract is indefinite. Customers may terminate at any time in text form, for example by email to {operator.email}. fogu may ordinarily terminate or discontinue the service on 90 days’ notice in text form; export remains available until the end. Statutory termination for good cause remains available. Necessary protective measures must be proportionate and secure return arranged. [IMPLEMENTATION REQUIRED: Access, complete export and erasure workflows must fulfil these commitments.] Technical erasure confirmation is distinct from termination: it starts seven days of read-only access with export/cancellation of the erasure instruction, followed by operator execution. It does not guarantee erasure exactly on day seven. Accounts are then disabled; no continuing archive access is offered. Statutory contract withdrawal remains separate.
draft.terms.liability.title: 9. Liability
draft.terms.liability.body: [COUNSEL WORDING REVIEW REQUIRED — Q10, including consumers.] fogu has unlimited liability for intent and gross negligence, culpable injury to life, body or health, fraudulent concealment of a defect and within the scope of an assumed guarantee. Mandatory liability under the Product Liability Act and liability under the GDPR, particularly Article 82, remain unaffected. For ordinary negligence in other cases, fogu is liable only for breach of an essential contractual duty whose performance enables proper fulfilment and on whose observance the customer may regularly rely; this liability is limited to foreseeable loss typical of the contract at conclusion. Outside these cases damages liability for ordinary negligence is excluded. This applies correspondingly to legal representatives and persons engaged to perform obligations. Statutory performance and cure claims, price reduction, termination and withdrawal are not restricted. There is no zero-euro cap, blanket data-loss exclusion or shortening of statutory limitation periods.
draft.terms.law.title: 10. Law and priority
draft.terms.law.body: German law applies. Consumers retain the protection of mandatory rules of the law applicable without this choice, particularly their habitual-residence country under Article 6 Rome I: https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2008/593/oj. Following approval the German text is authoritative. Individual agreements prevail; the DPA prevails for processing conflicts. No exclusive jurisdiction is agreed. Invalid clauses are handled under statutory rules, without automatic substitution by the economically closest provision.
draft.dpa.subject.title: 1. Parties, subject and duration
draft.dpa.subject.body: Processor: {operator.name}, {operator.street}, {operator.city}, {operator.country}, represented by {operator.director}, contact {operator.privacyEmail}. Customer: [full name, legal form, address, representative, contact and organization reference]. Subject: hosted Verwalino for rental, WEG and SEV management. Start: [date]; duration until the main agreement ends and return/erasure of remaining processing data is complete. Protection duties continue until then; no archive service is agreed. Private landlords and self-managing WEGs can also be controllers. Consumer status removes neither GDPR duties nor this DPA; letting is not exclusively personal or household activity (Articles 2(2)(c), 4(7) GDPR). For a manager, record actual role, representation and any upstream controllers and authorization. [IMPLEMENTATION REQUIRED: Versioned electronic conclusion at signup before first data entry.]
draft.dpa.purpose.title: 2. Annex 1 — nature and purpose
draft.dpa.purpose.body: Processing supports the commissioned property-management service: collection by entry/import, organization, storage, retrieval, calculation, preparation of statements and correspondence, instructed dispatch, export, backup/recovery, restriction and erasure. Documents are read locally; external analysis and property questions are performed on customer instruction through its own contracted AI provider under section 5 and Annex 3. Operational/support access is limited to what the assignment requires. No own advertising, sale or training of own models using processing data. For its own AI provider, the customer must contractually exclude training; actual provider terms still require review. fogu’s own account/contract and security purposes are separately described in the privacy notice.
draft.dpa.data.title: 3. Annex 1 — data categories
draft.dpa.data.body: Identity, address, communication and bank data; roles and user identifiers; leases, ownership, powers of attorney and service-provider contacts; rents, deposits, payments, arrears, bank movements, costs, invoices, statements, economic plans and asset reports; meter/consumption data; meeting, vote and resolution data; tasks, messages, signatures, uploaded and generated originals; editing, access, provenance and dispatch evidence. Approved AI use additionally covers transmitted questions, text/image extracts, results and usage data. Article 9/10 data is not an intended separate purpose but may occur in free text or attachments. [Customer-specific completion: Record necessary sensitive categories, permitted scope and additional safeguards; exclude unnecessary data. The owner’s DPIA/DPO assessment does not replace the customer’s assessment.]
draft.dpa.subjects.title: 4. Annex 1 — data subjects
draft.dpa.subjects.body: Tenants and co-tenants, owners and former owners, representatives and authorized agents, service providers and their contacts, customer employees/users, and other people mentioned in lawfully submitted records. [Before conclusion the customer must confirm actual groups, add particularly vulnerable groups where relevant, and remove unused groups.]
draft.dpa.duties.title: 5. Instructions, confidentiality and legality
draft.dpa.duties.body: fogu processes only on documented instructions, including transfers, unless EU or Member State law requires otherwise. It informs the customer beforehand unless legally prohibited for important public-interest reasons. Customer instruction contacts/deputies: [complete]. At fogu, Christian Kunkel handles instructions, rights requests, security and incidents. [TO SUPPLY Q12: absence deputy’s name.] Initial contact {operator.privacyEmail}; agree a protected channel for sensitive contents. Urgent oral instructions are documented promptly. If fogu considers an instruction unlawful, it informs the customer immediately and resolves the affected processing before continuing. Authorized persons are bound to confidentiality or statutory secrecy; access is limited to necessity. fogu maintains its record and cooperates with the competent authority. Q06 — customer-selected AI: AI functions are included at hosted launch. With the confirmation to be recorded when saving its own key, the customer instructs fogu to transmit the documents/text extracts, page images, questions and context necessary for the enabled functions to the provider it has selected and directly contracted. The customer is responsible for that provider’s Article 28 agreement, processing/support locations, retention and contractual exclusion of training. Under this model the provider is the customer’s own processor, not a sub-processor engaged by fogu. [COUNSEL REVIEW: Confirm this classification against actual contracts and processing, including private landlords and WEGs; a customer-supplied key alone does not establish it.] fogu remains responsible for documented instructions, appropriate transmission security under Article 32 and immediate notice of an instruction it considers unlawful under Article 28(3), last subparagraph; section 16 applies to its transfers. [IMPLEMENTATION REQUIRED #617: Record this instruction/confirmation in the app when the key is stored, before AI content processing. Current settings storage does not record this confirmation; the clause’s activation procedure depends on that implementation.]
draft.dpa.tom.title: 9. Annex 2 — safeguards and evidence status
draft.dpa.tom.body: fogu undertakes appropriate technical and organizational measures under Article 32 GDPR considering risk, state of the art and cost. The following distinguishes source capabilities/documented procedures from operational evidence; it does not prove deployment. [OPERATIONAL EVIDENCE REQUIRED: Christian Kunkel records implementation, responsibility, check date and private evidence for every measure.] Equivalent improvements may not reduce agreed protection. Material changes are documented and coordinated with the customer where agreed protection is affected. No certification is claimed.
draft.dpa.processors.title: 14. Annex 3 — recipients and sub-processor register
draft.dpa.processors.body: Before conclusion complete each entry: legal entity/address, task/data categories, storage/processing/support countries, further sub-processors, DPA/safeguard evidence, authorization/date, transfer basis and erasure period. Hosting: Contabo remains provider; the owner concludes its DPA before launch and verifies legal entity/address and access locations. [TO SUPPLY Q02: data-centre location from the contract.] Email: EU provider with DPA. [TO SUPPLY Q03: mail provider.] Backups: managed service of the same host under the same DPA. [TO SUPPLY Q04: backup product from the contract.] [TO SUPPLY Q04: retention of all backup copies from the contract.] Error tracking: self-hosted GlitchTip is documented; evidence actual hosting/access, with error reports retained 30 days from creation. Customer-selected AI (Q06): under the direct-contract model in section 5, this provider is the customer’s own processor and is not on fogu’s sub-processor list or subject to section 15 as such. Keep its identity, task/data, countries, retention, contract/training exclusion and transfer basis in a separate customer-specific recipient/instruction record. [COUNSEL REVIEW: Actual engagement and roles govern; if fogu engages a sub-processor, Article 28(2)/(4) and section 15 apply.] Technical support for OpenAI, Anthropic and OpenAI-compatible endpoints is not legal clearance of every endpoint. [IMPLEMENTATION REQUIRED #617: Recorded confirmation when storing the key; absent today.] Include maintenance services with possible data access; local OCR is not a sub-processor. Missing entries are not authorization; complete the register before use.
draft.dpa.controller.title: 8. Customer duties and audit rights
draft.dpa.controller.body: The customer is responsible for purposes, lawful bases, notices, lawful instructions and required upstream sub-processing authorization. fogu makes available all information demonstrating Article 28 compliance and allows and contributes to audits, including inspections, by the customer or its appointed auditor. Meaningful evidence may be reviewed first, without excluding necessary on-site inspection. Scope and timing are reasonably coordinated where the reason and urgency permit; incidents, justified suspicion or authority requirements are not subject to blanket annual or advance-notice limits. Other customers’ data and trade secrets are protected without frustrating the audit. This draft imposes no fee that prevents statutory audit or assistance.
draft.dpa.deletion.title: 17. Annex 4 — return, service exit and erasure
draft.dpa.deletion.body: At service end fogu provides a complete readable export of processing data due for return, then erases data and existing copies. Lawful customer instructions to erase without return remain possible (Article 28(3)(g) GDPR). Only a specific applicable statutory duty justifies residual storage with recorded category, provision, purpose, deadline and restricted access. Customer six/eight/ten-year statutory retention remains the customer’s task; no archive service is offered. Customers may terminate at any time; fogu gives 90 days’ ordinary notice, also for discontinuation, with export available until the end. [IMPLEMENTATION REQUIRED: Complete return, final erasure including remnants and backups, and verifiable execution.] Existing functionality is a permission-checked .tar.gz with JSONL, checksum manifest, originals and payment/cost CSV, downloadable for at most 24 hours; file cleanup is separate. Unauthorized evidence and credentials are omitted and re-import is limited. Technical erasure confirmation starts seven days of read-only access with export/cancellation; execution is then by the operator, not automatic on day seven. Accounts are disabled; some protected originals, evidence and dependencies remain without automatic final purge. These limitations do not justify indefinite retention. Backup copies follow the managed contractual period still to be evidenced in Annex 3; restores must reconcile later erasures. Server logs: 14 days, error reports: 30 days from creation, support: 90 days after closure; never-confirmed signups are cleaned up automatically. [IMPLEMENTATION REQUIRED: Traffic-independent cleanup and enforcement of these periods; current token expiry is not erasure evidence.] fogu records execution, remaining copies, reasons/periods and final completion.
draft.authoritative: Following approval, the German version is authoritative. This draft is not an executed contract or legal advice. [TO SUPPLY] identifies missing facts. [IMPLEMENTATION REQUIRED] and [COUNSEL REVIEW] are prerequisites for approval; Q06 is decided, but its recorded confirmation depends on issue #617.

draft.privacy.ai.title: 7. Optional document analysis and international transfers
draft.privacy.ai.body: Optional AI functions are included in the hosted launch model and operate only through a provider commissioned by the customer under its own contract and key. The customer instructs fogu to transmit the documents/text extracts, page images, questions and context needed for the selected analysis or property question to that provider. Under this model the provider is the customer’s own processor, not fogu’s sub-processor; the customer is responsible for its processing agreement, processing/support locations, retention and contractual exclusion of training. [COUNSEL REVIEW: Verify this role allocation against the actual contracts and processing, including private landlords and WEGs.] Current source allows the organization administrator to configure OpenAI, Anthropic or an OpenAI-compatible endpoint; OCR can run locally. No document contents or questions are sent for AI processing without a stored key; activation also requires a model and the relevant enabled function. Model discovery can contact the provider using a key entered before saving, without transmitting document contents or questions. [IMPLEMENTATION REQUIRED #617: Record the customer’s instruction/confirmation when saving the key; this confirmation is not currently recorded.] A customer-supplied key guarantees neither an EEA location nor zero retention. fogu remains responsible for its transmission security and statutory processor duties; if it performs a third-country transfer, Articles 44 onwards GDPR apply to it too. Before activation, document the actual recipients, countries, periods and transfer basis and make information on safeguards available; unresolved transfers are not permitted.
draft.privacy.security.title: 8. Security, error reporting and support
draft.privacy.security.body: Pseudonymous network/email keys limit login attempts; error reports support troubleshooting. Optional error tracking is off without a configured destination; self-hosted GlitchTip is documented for hosting. Filters reduce sensitive contents but do not anonymize remaining identifiers. Diagnostic bundles are shared manually; customer documents must not enter public error reports. The owner documents the Article 6(1)(f) balancing assessment for own security/support purposes. Error reports: 30 days from creation; closed support requests: 90 days after closure. Christian Kunkel and the deputy in section 1 are responsible. [IMPLEMENTATION REQUIRED: Evidence storage, access and timely cleanup; separately bound justified incident or claim evidence.]
draft.privacy.retention.title: 9. Retention and service exit
draft.privacy.retention.body: Accounts remain during use. Confirmation links last 24 hours; confirmed requests are removed. Never-confirmed signups are to be deleted automatically (Q05). Currently expired requests become cleanup-eligible seven days after expiry, with traffic-dependent execution. Reset links last one hour; token expiry is not guaranteed data erasure. [IMPLEMENTATION REQUIRED: Reliable traffic-independent cleanup with a bounded execution delay.] The decided backup policy uses Contabo’s managed backup service under the same DPA. [TO SUPPLY Q04: backup product from the contract.] [TO SUPPLY Q04: retention of all backup copies from the contract.] Activation and expiry of all copies still require evidence. At contract end the customer receives a complete export, followed by erasure; no archive service is offered. Customers may terminate at any time; fogu gives 90 days’ ordinary notice, with export until the end. [IMPLEMENTATION REQUIRED: Complete return, final erasure and backup cleanup.] The existing export is permission-filtered and downloadable for 24 hours. Technical erasure confirmation starts seven days of read-only access, followed by operator execution. Afterwards customer access ends, while some protected records/evidence remain without automatic final purge. These limitations are no legal basis for indefinite retention. The terms and DPA provide details.

draft.privacy.sources.body: Checked on 13 November 2026: GDPR, particularly Articles 5, 6, 12–22, 28, 32 and 44 onwards: https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2016/679/oj; section 25 TDDDG: https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/ttdsg/__25.html; section 38 BDSG: https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/bdsg_2018/__38.html. draft.terms.contract.title: 2. Contract formation and DPA
draft.terms.contract.body: At signup the customer or authorized representative electronically assents to the identified terms version and completed DPA with annexes before first management-data entry. Documents are readable and savable beforehand; contract content and accepted versions are confirmed on a durable medium before service begins. The contract starts with fogu’s confirmed acceptance. [IMPLEMENTATION REQUIRED: This assent and evidence step is missing; existing email confirmation is insufficient.] Privacy information is not blanket consent. Material contractual changes require a valid agreement; silence alone is not acceptance under these terms. Basis: section 305 BGB, section 312f BGB where distance-contract law applies, Article 28(9) GDPR.
draft.terms.retention.title: 8. Retention and erasure
draft.terms.retention.body: Complete export is followed by erasure including existing copies unless a specific applicable legal storage duty prevents it. Customers may instruct lawful erasure without prior return (Article 28(3)(g) GDPR). No archive service is offered. Any six/eight/ten-year category-specific retention under section 147 AO/section 257 HGB must be arranged by the customer outside the ended service; not every duty applies to every private landlord or WEG. Any own duty of fogu must identify category, provision, purpose, deadline and restricted access. [IMPLEMENTATION REQUIRED: Final erasure of protected remnants and every backup copy.] Current deletion guards and provisional periods create no additional statutory storage duty. The decided backup model uses the host under the contractual retention still to be evidenced; restoration must reconcile later erasures and access revocations before reopening.

GDPR of 27 April 2016: https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2016/679/oj. Retention: https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/ao_1977/__147.html; https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/hgb/__257.html. Contract classification, data purposes, consumer information and liability wording require counsel’s approval.
draft.dpa.assistance.title: 6. Rights and assistance
draft.dpa.assistance.body: Taking account of the nature of processing, fogu provides appropriate measures to assist with requests under Articles 12–22 GDPR. Customer-data requests received by fogu are forwarded promptly; fogu answers only on customer instructions unless it has its own legal duty. It provides available data and information in time for the customer’s deadlines and assists rectification, restriction, transfer and lawful erasure. Taking account of available information, it also assists Articles 32–36 duties, including risk assessment, DPIAs and prior consultation. A product export is not a substitute for a complete data-subject access response. Christian Kunkel and the absence deputy to be named in section 5 are responsible. Evidence reachability, authority and deadline tracking before processing begins; complete customer contacts privately.
draft.dpa.breach.title: 7. Personal-data breaches
draft.dpa.breach.body: fogu notifies the customer without undue delay after becoming aware of a breach affecting its processing data, without treating 72 hours as a waiting period. The initial notice includes available details of nature, affected data/subject categories and approximate numbers, contact, likely consequences and measures taken/proposed; missing information follows without undue further delay. fogu preserves necessary evidence, limits harm and assists notification/communication under Articles 33/34 GDPR. Decisions remain with the customer as controller; fogu’s own statutory duties remain unaffected. Christian Kunkel and the absence deputy to be named in section 5 are responsible. Evidence reachability, authority and deadline tracking before processing begins; complete customer contacts privately.
draft.dpa.tom_access.title: 10. Annex 2 — confidentiality and separation
draft.dpa.tom_access.body: Present in source: organization RLS and composite foreign keys; additional source/data-domain permissions; role checks and separate runtime/maintenance privileges; Argon2 password hashes; signed HttpOnly sessions revoked on relevant account changes; login limiting; local document storage and private export files. HTTPS with Caddy and SMTP TLS are documented operating paths. [OPERATIONAL EVIDENCE REQUIRED: Evidence TLS/Secure-cookie configuration, actual administrator rights, MFA for privileged operational access, access reviews, device security and host physical controls.] RLS does not prevent every privileged operator access. Full database/original encryption at rest or end-to-end encryption is not asserted as deployed.
draft.dpa.tom_integrity.title: 11. Annex 2 — integrity, traceability and minimization
draft.dpa.tom_integrity.body: Present: database guards against unlawful changes to confirmed financial data, original-file hash checks, editing/provenance evidence, permission-checked exports and bounded document processing. Error reports are scrubbed and secret fields are excluded from exports. Immutable evidence can remain personal data. [OPERATIONAL EVIDENCE REQUIRED: Evidence log access, detection/response, change approval, patch cadence and regular effectiveness checks.] A hash and technical immutability guard alone are not a GoBD attestation.
draft.dpa.tom_availability.title: 12. Annex 2 — availability and recovery
draft.dpa.tom_availability.body: The decided policy uses Contabo’s managed backup service under the same hosting DPA; product and retention are to be completed in Annex 3. [OPERATIONAL EVIDENCE REQUIRED: Contract and activation, database/document coverage, separation from server failure, encryption/key custody, schedule, expiry of all copies, recovery objectives and successful restoration.] The documented existing procedure initially stores same-server backups and rotates 14 daily/8 weekly unlabelled and ten labelled generations; this proves neither managed service nor a fixed maximum age. Erasures and access revocations after backup must be reconciled before reopening restored service. Automatic reconciliation is not asserted to exist.
draft.dpa.tom_organization.title: 13. Annex 2 — organization and rights
draft.dpa.tom_organization.body: Existing tools support access, permission-checked export, restriction and organization erasure with retention reconciliation. [OPERATIONAL EVIDENCE REQUIRED: Establish and evidence confidentiality commitments, training, access reviews, instruction/incident registers, supplier review, incident deputies and deadline tracking.] Retention expiry and deletion of final copies require a separate procedure; protected evidence currently has no automatic final purge. Evaluate effectiveness regularly and after material changes; provide the customer with necessary private evidence.
draft.dpa.changes.title: 15. Annex 3 — authorization and changes
draft.dpa.changes.body: The customer gives general written authorization based on the fully completed register at conclusion. fogu gives at least 30 days’ advance notice in text form of additions/replacements, with tasks, data, countries and safeguards; the customer may object on privacy grounds within 21 days of receipt. New-provider processing does not start before the notice period ends or while a justified objection remains unresolved. The parties seek an equivalent alternative. Without a solution the customer may end the affected service without charge; ordinary termination by fogu respects the main agreement’s 90-day notice and secure return. Statutory good-cause rights remain. Urgent departures need specific prior authorization. fogu imposes the same privacy duties on sub-processors and remains responsible to the customer for their performance (Article 28(4) GDPR). [IMPLEMENTATION REQUIRED: Direct versioned notices, deadlines and objection handling; merely editing a webpage is insufficient.]
draft.dpa.transfers.title: 16. Annex 3 — locations and international processing
draft.dpa.transfers.body: Hosting in Germany is not a promise that every data flow stays there. The Q06 customer remains responsible for its provider’s contract and locations. If fogu itself transmits or makes data available to a separate recipient in a third country, it remains subject to Chapter V as exporter even where the recipient is the customer’s own processor. A customer key, instruction or confirmation under #617 does not transfer those statutory duties to the customer. Processing or access outside the EU/EEA requires documented instructions/authorization and compliance with Articles 44 onwards GDPR. Before processing, record and make available the specific adequacy decision with verified scope or appropriate safeguards, including required transfer assessment and supplementary measures. Blanket customer consent does not replace this assessment. A flow is not approved while its recipient or basis remains unresolved.
draft.dpa.completion.title: 18. Conclusion and priority
draft.dpa.completion.body: Following approval the German version is authoritative; this agreement prevails over conflicting main-agreement provisions on processing. Statutory data-subject rights, supervisory powers and Article 82 GDPR remain unaffected. Changes and instructions are documented; Article 28(9) permits electronic form. Complete all open entries and annexes before conclusion; actual customer data, signatures and internal security evidence must not enter the public repository. draft.terms.liability_basis.title: Review basis for section 9
draft.terms.liability_basis.body: For counsel, as of 13 November 2026: section 276(3) BGB bars advance exclusion of intent; sections 307, 309 nos. 7 and 8, 310 BGB control standard-term exclusions, especially injury, gross fault and release rights. No. 8(b) concerns new goods/work and does not automatically cover SaaS. Section 327s(4) excludes damages limitations from its prohibition on derogation but preserves standard-terms control. Sections 521/599 privileges require defensible gift/loan classification; free pricing alone is insufficient. Their scope for this hosting contract and limits on essential duties remain unresolved. draft.terms.consumer.title: 11. Consumers and digital services
draft.terms.consumer.body: [COUNSEL REVIEW BEFORE CONSUMER LAUNCH: Confirm applicability against every actual data purpose.] If supplied personal data is processed exclusively to perform the service or meet legal requirements and for no other purpose, the section 312(1a) sentence 2 BGB exception applies, as referenced by section 327(3). Otherwise distance-contract and digital-product rules can apply despite EUR 0. Consumer standard-terms control applies independently. Where sections 327 onwards BGB apply, statutory provision and defect rights, including cure and where applicable termination, remain; necessary updates including security updates are owed throughout the agreed continuous provision period. Statutory rights on changes remain; these terms grant no general power to change performance adversely. draft.terms.information.title: 12. Pre-contract information
draft.terms.information.body: Provider, contact, management functions, limits, EUR 0 price, complaints, indefinite duration and termination are stated in sections 1–8 and the imprint. Access is online through a browser; internet access, JavaScript and the described login/storage functions are required. Exports use .tar.gz, JSONL, original files and CSV; import into arbitrary third-party systems is not promised. Protection uses login, permissions and organization separation. No additional guarantee is promised. Service begins after conclusion, contract confirmation and activation; no fixed activation time is promised. [APPROVAL PREREQUISITE: Verify actual compatibility, interoperability and activation flow; supply the telephone and deliver complete information before assent. Necessary software updates for continuous provision: throughout its agreed duration where section 327f BGB applies.] Where distance-contract law applies, confirm this information, withdrawal instructions/form and dispute-resolution information on a durable medium. draft.terms.withdrawal.title: 13. Withdrawal where distance-contract law applies — draft
draft.terms.withdrawal.body: [COUNSEL REVIEW: This consumer information covers the statutory variant described in section 11; identify its application clearly before approval.] You may withdraw within 14 days without giving a reason. The period starts on contract conclusion, but not before proper withdrawal information. Send an unambiguous statement to {operator.name}, {operator.street}, {operator.city}, email {operator.email}, telephone as stated in the imprint. The form below is optional. Sending before the deadline suffices. Withdrawal releases you from the contract; this gratuitous service entails no fees or compensation for service already performed. Data return and erasure follow mandatory law and the DPA; privacy rights remain. Without proper information the right generally expires at the latest twelve months and 14 days after conclusion. For a no-price service it also ends on full performance (section 356(5) no. 1 BGB); activation alone is not full performance of ongoing hosting. The separate rule for non-physical digital content (section 356(6) no. 1) is not used here to waive withdrawal for ongoing hosting. [IMPLEMENTATION REQUIRED: Where applicable, also provide the continuously accessible online withdrawal/confirmation function during the withdrawal period, with prompt acknowledgment on a durable medium, under section 356a BGB.] Sources: https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/bgb/__312g.html; https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/bgb/__355.html; https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/bgb/__356.html; https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/bgb/__356a.html; https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/bgb/__357a.html.
